column3: “The judgment belongs to you” is rendered “the judgment applies to you,” and “trap” “snare.”
The Hebrew is difficult; “slaughtering, rebels have made deep” is rendered “the revolters have gone deep in depravity,” and “I am discipline” “I will chastise.” The meaning is uncertain.
“In their inner being” is rendered “within them.”
“In its face” is rendered “against him”; NASB renders the future “will stumble” as present and perfect.
“After you” is rendered as a cry, “Behind you, Benjamin!”
“Waste” is rendered “desolation,” and “something trustworthy” “what is sure.”
“He walked after a command” is rendered “to follow man’s command”; NASB supplies “man’s.” The meaning of the Hebrew word is uncertain.
“King Jareb” follows the Hebrew; NASB renders “will not depart from you the wound” as “to cure you of your wound.”
“I, I” is rendered “I, even I”; NASB adds “away.”
“Be held guilty” is rendered “acknowledge their guilt,” and “when it is distress to them” “In their affliction.”
